title: Primary Function
learningObjectives: Connect crane function to mast load transfer.
student: State the primary function of the shop crane and the structural role of the vertical mast.
instructor: The crane lifts and positions heavy components. The mast participates in the frame load path, transferring demand from the boom and hydraulic system toward the base while carrying compression and receiving lateral restraint from the real braces.

title: External Loads
learningObjectives: Relate the suspended load to mast demand without equating them.
student: Identify the principal external load during lifting and explain how the boom and hydraulic system can transfer structural demand into the mast.
instructor: The suspended hook load acts on the boom. Boom, ram, joints, and braces redistribute forces into the mast and base, so the actual mast force is not generally identical to the hook load.

title: Supports and Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Distinguish real bracing from equivalent end conditions.
student: Identify real supports and restraints visible in the crane and distinguish them from the equivalent column end conditions used later.
instructor: The base, braces, boom-mast connection, and hydraulic/frame connections restrain the real mast. The pinned-pinned K = 1.0 condition is only an instructor-assigned equivalent model.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace lifting demand to the floor.
student: Trace the qualitative load path from the suspended load through the hook, boom, crane frame, base, and floor.
instructor: Demand travels from the hook into the boom, through the boom pivot and hydraulic/frame system into the mast and braces, then through the base and wheels or supports to the floor.

title: Critical Component
learningObjectives: Select the mast for stability analysis.
student: Identify the component selected for this problem and explain why a compression-member stability check is relevant.
instructor: The vertical mast is isolated because its equivalent axial compression makes column instability a relevant teaching check.

title: Relevant Mechanical Response
student: Identify the target failure mechanism and distinguish column buckling from a simple axial-stress calculation.
instructor: Buckling is a stability loss involving lateral deformation; it can govern before a simple uniform-stress limit in a sufficiently slender compression member.

title: Relevant Parameters
student: Identify the geometric, material, load, and restraint parameters controlling the assigned analysis.
instructor: P sets the applied demand; L and K define effective length; b, h, and t determine area and both centroidal inertias; E sets elastic stiffness.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
student: Draw an equivalent column showing axial P, modeled L, assumed end conditions, rectangular hollow cross section, and likely buckling direction.
instructor: A complete model shows a straight prismatic column, axial compression, equivalent pinned-pinned ends with K = 1.0, the assigned rectangular hollow section, and weak-axis lateral buckling.

title: Modeling Assumptions
student: State the assumptions used to reduce the real braced crane mast to the equivalent column model.
instructor: Use static equivalent axial loading, a straight prismatic rectangular hollow column, assigned L and geometry, linear elasticity, small initial deformation, Euler theory, and equivalent pinned-pinned K = 1.0. Neglect self-weight, connections, welds, ram and braces explicitly, frame interaction, eccentricity, residual stress, imperfections, local buckling, impact, fatigue, vibration, and dynamics.

title: Analysis Plan
student: Outline the calculation sequence before numerical work.
instructor: Calculate A, Ix, and Iy; select Imin and the weak axis; calculate rmin and KL/rmin; calculate Euler Pcr and the idealized load ratio; evaluate sensitivities; and interpret limitations.

title: Equivalent Column Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: State the equivalent end condition and K.
student: Using the assigned model, identify the equivalent end conditions and state K.
instructor: The teaching model is equivalent pinned-pinned with K = {{crane_mast_K}}. This is not a claim about literal real-crane joints.

title: Cross-Sectional Area
student: Calculate A = bh - (b - 2t)(h - 2t).
instructor: A = {{crane_mast_A_mm2}} mm2.

title: Centroidal Second Moments of Area
student: Calculate Ix and Iy for the rectangular hollow section.
instructor: Ix = {{crane_mast_Ix_mm4}} mm4 and Iy = {{crane_mast_Iy_mm4}} mm4.

title: Governing Buckling Axis
student: Determine Imin by comparing both axes and identify the expected weak-axis buckling direction.
instructor: Imin = {{crane_mast_Imin_mm4}} mm4, associated with {{crane_mast_axis}}.

title: Radius of Gyration
student: Calculate rmin = sqrt(Imin/A).
instructor: rmin = {{crane_mast_rmin_mm}} mm.

title: Slenderness Ratio
student: Calculate KL/rmin using consistent units and explain what it represents.
instructor: KL/rmin = {{crane_mast_slenderness}}. This moderate modeled slenderness is central to the limitation on interpreting classical Euler theory as a real failure prediction.

title: Euler Critical Buckling Load
student: Calculate Pcr = pi2EImin/(KL)2.
instructor: Pcr = {{crane_mast_Pcr_kN}} kN = {{crane_mast_Pcr_MN}} MN.

title: Idealized Buckling Margin
learningObjectives: Calculate and bound the Euler load ratio.
student: Calculate nb = Pcr/P and interpret it only within the equivalent Euler model.
instructor: nb = {{crane_mast_nb}}. This is an idealized Euler buckling margin, not the real crane's physical factor of safety.

title: Load Sensitivity
student: Increase P by 25%. Determine the new nb and explain why Pcr is unchanged.
instructor: Pnew = {{crane_mast_P25_kN}} kN; Pcr is unchanged because applied load is absent from the Euler capacity equation; nb,new = {{crane_mast_nb_P25}}.

title: Length Sensitivity
student: Increase L by 25%. Determine the new Pcr and nb, and explain the L-2 dependence.
instructor: Lnew = {{crane_mast_L25_m}} m, Pcr,new = {{crane_mast_Pcr_L25_kN}} kN, and nb,new = {{crane_mast_nb_L25}}.

title: Effective-Length Sensitivity
student: Set K = 2.0 with other inputs unchanged. Determine the new Pcr and nb, and explain the K-2 dependence.
instructor: Pcr,new = {{crane_mast_Pcr_K2_kN}} kN and nb,new = {{crane_mast_nb_K2}}.

title: Section Sensitivity
learningObjectives: Relate section dimensions to buckling resistance.
student: Explain how b, h, and t affect Ix, Iy, Imin, rmin, and Euler resistance. Why is material farther from the governing centroidal axis effective?
instructor: {{crane_mast_section_assessment}}

title: Euler-Model Applicability
student: Discuss why Euler buckling alone should not automatically be treated as the real mast failure load. Address slenderness, real bracing and restraint, imperfections and eccentricity, local buckling, yielding or inelastic behavior, and frame interaction.
instructor: With KL/r = {{crane_mast_slenderness}}, the assigned model has relatively low/moderate slenderness. Real bracing, non-ideal restraint, frame interaction, eccentricity, imperfections, residual stress, yielding or inelastic behavior, local wall buckling, connections, and hydraulic/boom interaction prevent treating Euler Pcr as a validated real failure load.

title: Engineering Assessment and Recommendation
student: State the governing idealized buckling axis, Pcr, nb, influential modeled parameters, one mechanics-based modification, and important model limitations. Do not claim crane certification.
instructor: {{crane_mast_assessment}}
